# wsgnstat

<!-- badges: start -->
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/mtloots/wsgnstat/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/mtloots/wsgnstat/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
[![CRAN status](https://www.r-pkg.org/badges/version/wsgnstat)](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=wsgnstat)
<!-- badges: end -->

The **skew generalised normal** distribution on the line and its **wrapping onto the circle**:
density, distribution and quantile functions, random generation, characteristic function,
trigonometric moments, and estimation by trigonometric moments or maximum likelihood. The
characteristic function is reached through absolutely convergent integrals rather than a series,
so every shape parameter is available. The computation runs on a pure-C back-end shared with the
Python package of the same name.

## Installation

From CRAN, once accepted:

```r
install.packages("wsgnstat")
```

The development version from GitHub:

```r
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("mtloots/wsgnstat", subdir = "wsgnstat")
```

## Example

Simulate from a skew member of the wrapped family, estimate its parameters, and compare with the
truth:

```{r example}
library(wsgnstat)
set.seed(1)
truth <- c(mu = 1, beta = 1.5, lam = 0.3)
theta <- rwsgn(1000, truth["mu"], truth["beta"], truth["lam"])
fit <- fit_wsgn_mle(theta)
round(rbind(truth = truth, estimate = fit$par), 3)
```

At shape 2 with `lam = 0.5` the circular law is the wrapped normal with sigma = 1/sqrt(2), and its
trigonometric moments are exactly exp(-p^2/4):

```{r anchor}
tm <- trig_moments(4, mu = 0, beta = 2, lam = 0.5)
rbind(engine = tm$A, closed_form = exp(-(1:4)^2 / 4))
```

The vignette, `vignette("wsgnstat")`, walks through the family, its reductions, estimation and an
application to wind directions.
